title: Unemployed teachers demonstrate for recruitment and teacher-pupil policy changes
location: Windhoek; route beyond the city is not confirmed
scope: A Windhoek gathering was reported; a national demonstration was announced beforehand but nationwide execution is unverified.
organizer: United Unemployment Teachers Movement (announced organizer), with Teachers Union of Namibia and Student Union of Namibia announced in solidarity; day-of presence is not specified.
threshold_50_evidence: The post-event report says 'dozens' without a count; this does not establish at least 50. The advance report's 1,980 unemployed teachers is a pool of jobseekers, not the gathering's attendance.

start_date.summary: The advance report schedules the action for Thursday; the next-day report dated 22 January says it happened Thursday, corresponding to 21 January.

end_date.summary: No end time or physical closure reported; left unknown.

location.summary: The post-event report places the gathering in Windhoek and says a petition went to the prime minister; the advance article lists a planned route.

scope.summary: National scope was announced, but post-event reporting confirms only a Windhoek gathering.

organizer.summary: UUTM, TUN and SUN are named in the advance notice; day-of presence of each is not confirmed.

demands.summary: Demands concerned government teacher-pupil policy and Ministry recruitment procedures; coded political_behavior_process, not a wage dispute.

participants_original.summary: The report says 'dozens'; no precise number.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be derived from 'dozens'.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: At least 50 not established. The 1,980 figure describes unemployed teachers in several regions, not people at this event.

state_accommodation.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_arrests.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_beatings.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_ignore.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_killings.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

state_shootings.summary: No state response information reported; left unknown, and silence is not coded as ignore.

eligibility.summary: Domestic state-policy demand is clear; public attendance of 50 remains unproven.

notes: A prior-year teacher protest is mentioned but no evidence yet establishes continuity. The January gathering is retained because it occurred and had a state-policy target; its threshold remains unproven.
open_questions: Can another contemporary report establish attendance of at least 50?
Were other towns involved on 21 January?
Was this a fresh event or continuous with a 2020 teacher campaign?
Was any state response reported beyond petition receipt?

title: Oshakati police-station release demand during the Shoprite strike
location: Oshakati police station; the later return to Yetu Complex is documented as a separate phase
scope: This candidate covers the police-station gathering demanding release of Leonard Indongo after his arrest. The later Yetu Complex crowd is a separate reported phase; crowd identity, overlap and attendance at the state-demand gathering are unresolved.
organizer: Shoprite strikers, NAFAU officials and Affirmative Repositioning activists appear in accounts of the sequence; the organizer and attendance of the police-station release-demand gathering are unspecified.
participants_original: Demonstrators at the police station; no count reported. The later Yetu Complex crowd is not treated as the same count.
threshold_50_evidence: No report gives attendance for the police-station release-demand gathering. The later Yetu Complex crowd has no separate count either; injuries at that phase are not attendance at the station phase. At least 50 at the state-demand gathering is unproven.

start_date.summary: Reports date the Oshakati confrontation to Friday 15 January; the 18 January report says Friday evening.

end_date.summary: The report describes a return to Yetu Complex and later confrontation but not when people physically dispersed; unknown.

location.summary: The state-directed release demand is reported at the police station after Indongo’s arrest; sources then describe a return to Yetu Complex and a later confrontation. Phase overlap is unresolved.

scope.summary: Local Oshakati gathering; people from nearby towns were allegedly brought in but no total is given.

organizer.summary: Strikers, NAFAU officials and AR activists are reported in the action; exact organizer of the release demand is unclear.

demands.summary: The state-directed demand occurred at the police station after Indongo’s arrest: demonstrators demanded his immediate release. It is distinct from the private-employer wage demand; taxonomy assignment remains unresolved.

participants_original.summary: The candidate is scoped to station demonstrators. Reports describe a separate later Yetu Complex crowd but do not count either phase or establish whether membership was the same.

participants_min.summary: No attendance count for the state-demand station gathering or later Yetu crowd.

participants_max.summary: No attendance count for either reported phase.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The station release-demand gathering and later Yetu Complex crowd are not separately counted; injuries do not establish attendance at the station phase.

protester_violence.summary: Police alleged stones were thrown; other accounts allege police initiated force. Conflicting accounts leave protester violence unknown.

state_accommodation.summary: No negotiation or release is reported at the station; response to the station demand is unknown.

state_arrests.summary: Indongo’s arrest preceded and motivated the station release-demand gathering; it is not coded as an arrest response to that gathering.

state_crowd_dispersal.summary: Police dispersal is reported at the later Yetu Complex phase. The evidence does not establish that it was a response to the candidate’s earlier police-station release demand; candidate-level response remains unknown.

state_ignore.summary: Police action is reported at Yetu Complex; this does not establish the state’s response to the earlier station demand.

state_killings.summary: Injuries are reported in the later Yetu Complex confrontation; no death is attributed to either phase.

state_shootings.summary: Rubber-bullet fire is reported for the later Yetu Complex confrontation. The evidence does not link that force to the earlier station release demand; candidate-level shooting response remains unknown, and no live ammunition is reported.

eligibility.summary: The release request at the police station was directed to domestic police/state, distinct from the private wage grievance. At least 50 participants at this gathering is unproven; later Yetu force is not used to establish eligibility or response.

notes: Candidate is scoped to the state-directed police-station demand for release after Indongo’s arrest. Informanté separates the earlier Shoprite march/arrest, station demand, return to Yetu Complex and later confrontation. Rubber bullets and dispersal are retained as reported facts about the later Yetu phase only; a response to the station demand is not established. The relation between the state-directed demand and the December-started private-employer wage strike remains unresolved.
open_questions: Can attendance at the station release-demand gathering be established as at least 50, separately from the later Yetu Complex crowd?
Do reports establish whether the police-station and Yetu Complex crowds were the same people or one continuous gathering?
Is the release demand a distinct protest or a local action within the December-started strike?
Which fixed demand category, if any, fits the request to release the arrested activist?
Can independent evidence confirm rubber-bullet use and circumstances at the later Yetu Complex phase?
When did each phase physically disperse?

title: Windhoek unemployed-teacher demonstration and petition (reported 19 January)
scope: The report identifies a Windhoek street demonstration; route and broader geographic participation are not specified.
organizer: Unemployed graduate teachers; the report does not name an organizing body for this date.
threshold_50_evidence: The report says “scores” without a numerical estimate; this does not establish that at least 50 people attended. The separate “more than 200” figure in the same article refers to interviewees in Ohangwena, not this gathering.

start_date.summary: The 2 February report explicitly dates the Windhoek street demonstration to 19 January.

end_date.summary: No end time or physical closure reported; unknown.

location.summary: The report says unemployed graduates took to the streets of Windhoek.

scope.summary: Windhoek gathering only; route and any other locations not stated.

organizer.summary: Participants are described as unemployed graduate teachers; a named organizer is not identified.

demands.summary: The group is described as protesting unemployment and handing a petition with demands to the Office of the Prime Minister. This article does not restate the Jan19 petition’s contents; demand categories remain unassigned.

participants_original.summary: The article says “scores”; it does not provide a numeric count.

participants_min.summary: No numeric minimum can be derived from “scores”.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: At least 50 is unproven. The over-200 interviewee count concerns Ohangwena candidates and must not be assigned to this Windhoek gathering.

state_accommodation.summary: A later letter from the PM assistant describes consultations but is not tied to this gathering alone; unknown.

state_ignore.summary: No response reported; silence is not coded as ignore.

eligibility.summary: The source reports a public gathering and petition to the Office of the Prime Minister; the contents of this petition and attendance count remain unresolved, so keep pending review.

notes: The 2 February account names 19 January, while advance and post-event coverage supports a separate announced/reported 21 January action. Keep this candidate distinct pending evidence on whether these were separate gatherings or one date error. The source’s “more than 200” figure concerns interview-selected teachers in Ohangwena, not the Windhoek protest. Do not infer the Jan19 petition contents or assign the later PM letter to this date alone.
open_questions: Was the 19 January demonstration separate from the 21 January reported action, or is one date erroneous?
Can attendance at the 19 January gathering be established as at least 50?
What were the specific demands on the Jan19 petition?
Can any state response be linked to this gathering rather than the Jan21 action?
